sanskrit: sa taṃ dvipaṃ sahasābhyāpatantam; avidhyad arkapratimaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ karmāradhautair niśitair jvaladbhir; nārācamukhyais tribhir ugravegaiḥ
english: As that elephant came rushing suddenly upon him, he pierced it with arrows bright as the sun—three foremost iron shafts, keen, blazing, burnished by the smith, and terrible in their speed.

sanskrit: tato 'parān pañca śitān mahātmā; nārācamukhyān visasarja kumbhe sa tais tu viddhaḥ paramadvipo raṇe; tadā parāvṛtya bhṛśaṃ pradudruve
english: Then the great-souled one loosed five more sharpened iron shafts into the beast's frontal lobes; and that foremost of elephants, sorely struck by them in battle, wheeled about and fled away in haste.

sanskrit: taṃ nāgarājaṃ sahasā praṇunnaṃ; vidrāvyamāṇaṃ ca nigṛhya śālvaḥ tottrāṅkuśaiḥ preṣayām āsa tūrṇaṃ; pāñcālarājasya rathaṃ pradiśya
english: But Śālva, seizing that lord of elephants as it was suddenly driven back and put to flight, with goad and hook urged it swiftly forward, directing it against the chariot of the Pāñcāla king.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvāpatantaṃ sahasā tu nāgaṃ; dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ svarathāc chīghram eva gadāṃ pragṛhyāśu javena vīro; bhūmiṃ prapanno bhayavihvalāṅgaḥ
english: Seeing the elephant suddenly bearing down on him, the hero Dhṛṣṭadyumna swiftly seized his mace and leapt down at once from his own chariot, his limbs trembling with fear, and set foot upon the ground.

sanskrit: sa taṃ rathaṃ hemavibhūṣitāṅgaṃ; sāśvaṃ sasūtaṃ sahasā vimṛdya utkṣipya hastena tadā mahādvipo; vipothayām āsa vasuṃdharātale
english: That mighty elephant crushed in an instant the chariot adorned with gold, together with its horses and driver, and lifting it up with its trunk dashed it down upon the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: pāñcālarājasya sutaṃ sa dṛṣṭvā; tadārditaṃ nāgavareṇa tena tam abhyadhāvat sahasā javena; bhīmaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca śineś ca naptā
english: Seeing the son of the Pāñcāla king thus hard-pressed by that foremost of elephants, Bhīma, Śikhaṇḍin, and the grandson of Śini rushed upon it at once with great speed.

sanskrit: śaraiś ca vegaṃ sahasā nigṛhya; tasyābhito 'bhyāpatato gajasya sa saṃgṛhīto rathibhir gajo vai; cacāla tair vāryamāṇaś ca saṃkhye
english: Checking with their arrows the onrushing charge of the elephant that bore down upon them, those chariot-warriors held the beast in their grip; and so beset and stayed by them in battle, it staggered.

sanskrit: tataḥ pṛṣatkān pravavarṣa rājā; sūryo yathā raśmijālaṃ samantāt tenāśugair vadhyamānā rathaughāḥ; pradudruvus tatra tatas tu sarve
english: Then the king rained down his shafts on every side, as the sun pours forth its web of rays; and the hosts of chariots, smitten by those swift arrows, fled away in all directions.

sanskrit: tat karma śālvasya samīkṣya sarve; pāñcālamatsyā nṛpa sṛñjayāś ca hāhākārair nādayantaḥ sma yuddhe; dvipaṃ samantād rurudhur narāgryāḥ
english: Beholding that feat of Śālva, O king, all the Pāñcālas, Matsyas, and Sṛñjayas—foremost of men—filling the battle with cries of dismay, hemmed in the elephant on every side.

sanskrit: pāñcālarājas tvaritas tu śūro; gadāṃ pragṛhyācalaśṛṅgakalpām asaṃbhramaṃ bhārata śatrughātī; javena vīro 'nusasāra nāgam
english: But the valiant king of the Pāñcālas, slayer of foes, swiftly grasping a mace like the peak of a mountain, O descendant of Bharata, pursued the elephant with speed, the hero unshaken and unafraid.

sanskrit: tato 'tha nāgaṃ dharaṇīdharābhaṃ; madaṃ sravantaṃ jaladaprakāśam gadāṃ samāvidhya bhṛśaṃ jaghāna; pāñcālarājasya sutas tarasvī
english: Then the swift son of the Pāñcāla king, whirling his mace, struck mightily that elephant which was like a mountain bearing the earth, dark as a rain-cloud, and streaming with rut.

sanskrit: sa bhinnakumbhaḥ sahasā vinadya; mukhāt prabhūtaṃ kṣatajaṃ vimuñcan papāta nāgo dharaṇīdharābhaḥ; kṣitiprakampāc calito yathādriḥ
english: Its frontal lobes shattered, the elephant, vast as a mountain, suddenly bellowed and, vomiting a great gush of blood from its mouth, fell to earth like a peak shaken loose by an earthquake.

sanskrit: nipātyamāne tu tadā gajendre; hāhākṛte tava putrasya sainye sa śālvarājasya śinipravīro; jahāra bhallena śiraḥ śitena
english: As that lordly elephant was being brought down, and your son's host raised its cry of dismay, the hero of Śini's line struck off, with a keen broad-headed shaft, the head of King Śālva.

sanskrit: hṛtottamāṅgo yudhi sātvatena; papāta bhūmau saha nāgarājñā yathādriśṛṅgaṃ sumahat praṇunnaṃ; vajreṇa devādhipacoditena
english: His head struck off in battle by the Sātvata, he fell to the ground together with the lordly elephant, like a great mountain-peak shattered and hurled down by the thunderbolt sped by the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmiṃs tu nihate śūre śālve samitiśobhane tavābhajyad balaṃ vegād vāteneva mahādrumaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When that valiant Śālva, the ornament of the assembly of battle, was slain, your host broke apart in headlong flight, as a great tree is shattered by the wind.

sanskrit: tat prabhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ dadhāra samare śūraḥ śatrusainyaṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Seeing that host put to rout, the great chariot-warrior Kṛtavarman, valiant and of mighty strength, held back the army of the foe in battle.

sanskrit: saṃnivṛttās tu te śūrā dṛṣṭvā sātvatam āhave śailopamaṃ sthitaṃ rājan kīryamāṇaṃ śarair yudhi
english: Then those warriors turned back, beholding the Sātvata standing firm in the fray like a mountain, O king, though showered over with arrows in the fight.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha nivṛttānāṃ mahārāja mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: Then the battle was joined afresh between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, O great king—the Kurus who had turned back, having made death itself the price of their return.

sanskrit: tatrāścaryam abhūd yuddhaṃ sātvatasya paraiḥ saha yad eko vārayām āsa pāṇḍusenāṃ durāsadām
english: Wondrous there was the battle of the Sātvata with the foe, in that he alone held back the invincible army of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: teṣām anyonyasuhṛdāṃ kṛte karmaṇi duṣkare siṃhanādaḥ prahṛṣṭānāṃ divaḥspṛk sumahān abhūt
english: When that hard deed was done by him, the lion-roar of those exultant comrades, fond friends each of the other, rose vast enough to touch the heavens.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastān pāñcālān bharatarṣabha śiner naptā mahābāhur anvapadyata sātyakiḥ
english: The Pāñcālas, terrified by that sound, O bull of the Bhāratas, the mighty-armed Sātyaki, grandson of Śini, came up in support of.

sanskrit: sa samāsādya rājānaṃ kṣemadhūrtiṃ mahābalam saptabhir niśitair bāṇair anayad yamasādanam
english: Closing with the mighty king Kṣemadhūrti, he sent him with seven keen arrows to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tam āyāntaṃ mahābāhuṃ pravapantaṃ śitāñ śarān javenābhyapatad dhīmān hārdikyaḥ śinipuṃgavam
english: As that mighty-armed bull of Śini's line came on, scattering sharp arrows, the sagacious son of Hṛdika fell upon him with speed.

sanskrit: tau siṃhāv iva nardantau dhanvinau rathināṃ varau anyonyam abhyadhāvetāṃ śastrapravaradhāriṇau
english: Those two bowmen, foremost of chariot-warriors, roaring like lions and bearing the choicest of weapons, rushed each upon the other.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāḥ saha pāñcālair yodhāś cānye nṛpottamāḥ prekṣakāḥ samapadyanta tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas with the Pāñcālas, and the other warriors, those best of kings, became spectators of those two lions among men.

sanskrit: nārācair vatsadantaiś ca vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathau abhijaghnatur anyonyaṃ prahṛṣṭāv iva kuñjarau
english: With iron shafts and calf-toothed arrows the two great chariot-warriors of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas struck at each other, like two rutting elephants in their joy of battle.

sanskrit: carantau vividhān mārgān hārdikyaśinipuṃgavau muhur antardadhāte tau bāṇavṛṣṭyā parasparam
english: Ranging through manifold courses of fight, the son of Hṛdika and the bull of Śini's line again and again hid each other from view beneath a rain of arrows.

sanskrit: cāpavegabaloddhūtān mārgaṇān vṛṣṇisiṃhayoḥ ākāśe samapaśyāma pataṃgān iva śīghragān
english: We saw the shafts of those two lions of the Vṛṣṇis, driven up by the force and might of their bows, speeding swift as locusts through the sky.

sanskrit: tam ekaṃ satyakarmāṇam āsādya hṛdikātmajaḥ avidhyan niśitair bāṇaiś caturbhiś caturo hayān
english: Closing with that lone hero of true deeds, the son of Hṛdika pierced his four horses with four keen arrows.

sanskrit: sa dīrghabāhuḥ saṃkruddhas tottrārdita iva dvipaḥ aṣṭābhiḥ kṛtavarmāṇam avidhyat parameṣubhiḥ
english: Then that long-armed hero, enraged like an elephant stung by the goad, pierced Kṛtavarman with eight excellent shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭaiḥ kṛtavarmā śilāśitaiḥ sātyakiṃ tribhir āhatya dhanur ekena cicchide
english: Then Kṛtavarman, with arrows whetted on stone and loosed from a fully drawn bow, struck Sātyaki with three and with one severed his bow.

sanskrit: nikṛttaṃ tad dhanuḥśreṣṭham apāsya śinipuṃgavaḥ anyad ādatta vegena śaineyaḥ saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
english: Casting aside that excellent bow now cut asunder, the bull of Śini's line, the grandson of Śini, swiftly took up another bow with an arrow already fitted.

sanskrit: tad ādāya dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ variṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanvinām āropya ca mahāvīryo mahābuddhir mahābalaḥ
english: Taking up that excellent bow, the best of all bowmen, of mighty valor, mighty wisdom, and mighty strength, strung it.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇo dhanuṣaś chedanaṃ kṛtavarmaṇā kupito 'tirathaḥ śīghraṃ kṛtavarmāṇam abhyayāt
english: Unable to brook the cutting of his bow by Kṛtavarman, that surpassing chariot-warrior, in his wrath, swiftly bore down upon Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: tataḥ suniśitair bāṇair daśabhiḥ śinipuṃgavaḥ jaghāna sūtam aśvāṃś ca dhvajaṃ ca kṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: Then with ten well-sharpened arrows the bull of Śini's line slew the driver, the horses, and the banner of Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: tato rājan maheṣvāsaḥ kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ hatāśvasūtaṃ saṃprekṣya rathaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam
english: Then, O king, the great bowman Kṛtavarman, that mighty chariot-warrior, beheld his chariot wrought with gold, its horses and driver slain.

sanskrit: roṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭaḥ śūlam udyamya māriṣa cikṣepa bhujavegena jighāṃsuḥ śinipuṃgavam
english: Seized by great wrath, O sire, he raised a lance and hurled it with the force of his arm, eager to slay the bull of Śini's line.

sanskrit: tac chūlaṃ sātvato hy ājau nirbhidya niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ cūrṇitaṃ pātayām āsa mohayann iva mādhavam tato 'pareṇa bhallena hṛdy enaṃ samatāḍayat
english: But the Sātvata in battle, splitting that lance with keen arrows, brought it down shattered to pieces, as though to confound the Mādhava; and then with another broad-headed shaft he struck him upon the breast.

sanskrit: sa yuddhe yuyudhānena hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ kṛtavarmā kṛtāstreṇa dharaṇīm anvapadyata
english: His horses slain and his charioteer slain in battle by Yuyudhāna, accomplished in arms, Kṛtavarman sank down upon the earth.

sanskrit: tasmin sātyakinā vīre dvairathe virathīkṛte samapadyata sarveṣāṃ sainyānāṃ sumahad bhayam
english: When that hero was unhorsed by Sātyaki in their single chariot-duel, a very great fear came upon all the host.

sanskrit: putrasya tava cātyarthaṃ viṣādaḥ samapadyata hatasūte hatāśve ca virathe kṛtavarmaṇi
english: And exceeding great was the despondency that came upon your son when Kṛtavarman, his driver slain and his horses slain, was robbed of his chariot.

sanskrit: hatāśvaṃ ca samālakṣya hatasūtam ariṃdamam abhyadhāvat kṛpo rājañ jighāṃsuḥ śinipuṃgavam
english: Marking that tamer of foes with his horses slain and his driver slain, Kṛpa rushed forward, O king, eager to slay the bull of Śini's line.

sanskrit: tam āropya rathopasthe miṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām apovāha mahābāhus tūrṇam āyodhanād api
english: Lifting him up into the seat of his chariot, before the eyes of all the bowmen, the mighty-armed one swiftly bore him away even from the field of battle.

sanskrit: śaineye 'dhiṣṭhite rājan virathe kṛtavarmaṇi duryodhanabalaṃ sarvaṃ punar āsīt parāṅmukham
english: When the grandson of Śini held the field, O king, and Kṛtavarman was bereft of his chariot, the whole host of Duryodhana once more turned its face away in flight.

sanskrit: tatpare nāvabudhyanta sainyena rajasāvṛte tāvakāḥ pradrutā rājan duryodhanam ṛte nṛpam
english: The foe did not perceive it, the host being veiled in dust; and your men fled away, O king, save only King Duryodhana.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu saṃprekṣya bhagnaṃ svabalam antikāt javenābhyapatat tūrṇaṃ sarvāṃś caiko nyavārayat
english: But Duryodhana, beholding his own host broken close at hand, dashed forward swiftly with speed and alone held back them all.

sanskrit: pāṇḍūṃś ca sarvān saṃkruddho dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam śikhaṇḍinaṃ draupadeyān pāñcālānāṃ ca ye gaṇāḥ
english: In wrath he checked all the Pāṇḍavas, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata, and Śikhaṇḍin, and the sons of Draupadī, and the bands of the Pāñcālas,

sanskrit: kekayān somakāṃś caiva pāñcālāṃś caiva māriṣa asaṃbhramaṃ durādharṣaḥ śitair astrair avārayat
english: and the Kekayas and the Somakas and the Pāñcālas too, O sire; unflinching and unassailable, he held them back with keen weapons.

sanskrit: atiṣṭhad āhave yattaḥ putras tava mahābalaḥ yathā yajñe mahān agnir mantrapūtaḥ prakāśayan
english: Your mighty son stood intent in the fray, blazing forth like the great fire of the sacrifice, hallowed by sacred chants.

sanskrit: taṃ pare nābhyavartanta martyā mṛtyum ivāhave athānyaṃ ratham āsthāya hārdikyaḥ samapadyata
english: The foe could not stand against him in battle, as mortals cannot stand against death; and meanwhile the son of Hṛdika, mounting another chariot, came up once more.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca putras tu te mahārāja rathastho rathināṃ varaḥ durutsaho babhau yuddhe yathā rudraḥ pratāpavān
english: Saṃjaya said: Your son, O great king, foremost of chariot-warriors, standing in his car, shone irresistible in battle like the glowing Rudra.

sanskrit: tasya bāṇasahasrais tu pracchannā hy abhavan mahī parāṃś ca siṣice bāṇair dhārābhir iva parvatān
english: By his thousands of arrows the earth was covered over, and he drenched the foe with shafts as rain-streams drench the mountains.

sanskrit: na ca so 'sti pumān kaś cit pāṇḍavānāṃ mahāhave hayo gajo ratho vāpi yo 'sya bāṇair avikṣataḥ
english: There was no man among the Pāṇḍavas in that great battle, nor horse, nor elephant, nor chariot, that was left unwounded by his arrows.

sanskrit: yaṃ yaṃ hi samare yodhaṃ prapaśyāmi viśāṃ pate sa sa bāṇaiś cito 'bhūd vai putreṇa tava bhārata
english: Whatever warrior I beheld in the fight, O lord of peoples, that one was found covered over with arrows by your son, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: yathā sainyena rajasā samuddhūtena vāhinī pratyadṛśyata saṃchannā tathā bāṇair mahātmanaḥ
english: As an army appears veiled in the dust raised by its own host, so did the host appear shrouded by the arrows of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: bāṇabhūtām apaśyāma pṛthivīṃ pṛthivīpate duryodhanena prakṛtāṃ kṣiprahastena dhanvinā
english: We saw the earth become all arrows, O lord of the earth, made so by Duryodhana, that bowman of nimble hand.

sanskrit: teṣu yodhasahasreṣu tāvakeṣu pareṣu ca eko duryodhano hy āsīt pumān iti matir mama
english: Among those thousands of warriors, your own and the foe's alike, Duryodhana alone was a man indeed—such is my judgment.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma tava putrasya vikramam yad ekaṃ sahitāḥ pārthā nātyavartanta bhārata
english: There we beheld the wondrous prowess of your son, in that the sons of Pṛthā, all united, could not overcome him single-handed, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ śatenājau vivyādha bharatarṣabha bhīmasenaṃ ca saptatyā sahadevaṃ ca saptabhiḥ
english: He pierced Yudhiṣṭhira in battle with a hundred shafts, O bull of the Bhāratas, and Bhīmasena with seventy, and Sahadeva with seven,

sanskrit: nakulaṃ ca catuḥṣaṣṭyā dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ saptabhir draupadeyāṃś ca tribhir vivyādha sātyakim dhanuś ciccheda bhallena sahadevasya māriṣa
english: and Nakula with sixty-four, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna with five, and the sons of Draupadī with seven, and Sātyaki with three; and with a broad-headed shaft he cut asunder the bow of Sahadeva, O sire.

sanskrit: tad apāsya dhanuś chinnaṃ mādrīputraḥ pratāpavān abhyadhāvata rājānaṃ pragṛhyānyan mahad dhanuḥ tato duryodhanaṃ saṃkhye vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Casting aside that broken bow, the valiant son of Mādrī took up another great bow and rushed upon the king; then in the fight he pierced Duryodhana with ten arrows.

sanskrit: nakulaś ca tato vīro rājānaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ ghorarūpair maheṣvāso vivyādha ca nanāda ca
english: And then the hero Nakula, that great bowman, pierced the king with nine arrows of dreadful form, and raised a shout.

sanskrit: sātyakiś cāpi rājānaṃ śareṇānataparvaṇā draupadeyās trisaptatyā dharmarājaś ca saptabhiḥ aśītyā bhīmasenaś ca śarai rājānam ārdayat
english: Sātyaki too struck the king with a smooth-jointed shaft, and the sons of Draupadī with seventy-three, and the king of righteousness with seven, and Bhīmasena tormented the king with eighty arrows.

sanskrit: samantāt kīryamāṇas tu bāṇasaṃghair mahātmabhiḥ na cacāla mahārāja sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: Though showered on every side with masses of arrows by those great-souled ones, he did not waver, O great king, while all the host looked on.

sanskrit: lāghavaṃ sauṣṭhavaṃ cāpi vīryaṃ caiva mahātmanaḥ ati sarvāṇi bhūtāni dadṛśuḥ sarvamānavāḥ
english: The deftness, the dexterity, and the valor of that great-souled one—all beings, all men, beheld them surpassing all.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrās tu rājendra yātvā tu svalpam antaram apaśyamānā rājānaṃ paryavartanta daṃśitāḥ
english: But the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O lord of kings, having gone but a little way, and seeing not their king, turned back, clad once more in their mail.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ ghoras tumulaḥ samajāyata kṣubdhasya hi samudrasya prāvṛṭkāle yathā niśi
english: As they came rushing on, a terrible tumult arose, like that of the troubled ocean by night in the season of rains.

sanskrit: samāsādya raṇe te tu rājānam aparājitam pratyudyayur maheṣvāsāḥ pāṇḍavān ātatāyinaḥ
english: Rejoining the unconquered king in battle, those great bowmen advanced to meet the Pāṇḍavas, who came on with weapons raised to slay.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ raṇe kruddhaṃ droṇaputro nyavārayat tato bāṇair mahārāja pramuktaiḥ sarvatodiśam nājñāyanta raṇe vīrā na diśaḥ pradiśas tathā
english: The son of Droṇa held back Bhīmasena, enraged in battle; and then, O great king, by the arrows loosed on every side, neither the heroes nor the quarters nor the intermediate points could be discerned in the fray.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau krūrakarmāṇāv ubhau bhārata duḥsahau ghorarūpam ayudhyetāṃ kṛtapratikṛtaiṣiṇau trāsayantau jagat sarvaṃ jyākṣepavihatatvacau
english: Those two, both grim in their deeds, both hard to bear, O descendant of Bharata, fought in dreadful fashion, each seeking to repay blow with blow, terrifying the whole world, the skin of their forearms torn by the lashing of their bowstrings.

sanskrit: śakunis tu raṇe vīro yudhiṣṭhiram apīḍayat tasyāśvāṃś caturo hatvā subalasya suto vibhuḥ nādaṃ cakāra balavān sarvasainyāni kampayan
english: But the hero Śakuni in battle pressed Yudhiṣṭhira hard; and the mighty lord, the son of Subala, having slain his four horses, raised a roar that made all the hosts tremble.

sanskrit: etasminn antare vīraṃ rājānam aparājitam apovāha rathenājau sahadevaḥ pratāpavān
english: In that interval the valiant Sahadeva bore away the unconquered king, the hero, from the battle upon his own chariot.

sanskrit: athānyaṃ ratham āsthāya dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śakuniṃ navabhir viddhvā punar vivyādha pañcabhiḥ nanāda ca mahānādaṃ pravaraḥ sarvadhanvinām
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, king of righteousness, mounting another chariot, pierced Śakuni with nine shafts and again with five, and that foremost of all bowmen sent forth a mighty roar.

sanskrit: tad yuddham abhavac citraṃ ghorarūpaṃ ca māriṣa īkṣitṛprītijananaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam
english: Wondrous was that battle, and dreadful of form, O sire, delighting the hearts of the onlookers, and graced by the presence of the Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: ulūkas tu maheṣvāsaṃ nakulaṃ yuddhadurmadam abhyadravad ameyātmā śaravarṣaiḥ samantataḥ
english: But Ulūka, of measureless spirit, rushed upon the great bowman Nakula, that frenzied warrior, with showers of arrows on every side.

sanskrit: tathaiva nakulaḥ śūraḥ saubalasya sutaṃ raṇe śaravarṣeṇa mahatā samantāt paryavārayat
english: And in like manner the valiant Nakula, in battle, hemmed in the son of Subala on every side with a great shower of arrows.

sanskrit: tau tatra samare vīrau kulaputrau mahārathau yodhayantāv apaśyetāṃ parasparakṛtāgasau
english: Those two heroes there in battle, scions of noble houses and mighty chariot-warriors, were seen fighting on, each having wronged the other.

sanskrit: tathaiva kṛtavarmā tu śaineyaṃ śatrutāpanam yodhayañ śuśubhe rājan balaṃ śakra ivāhave
english: And so too Kṛtavarman, fighting the grandson of Śini, that scorcher of foes, shone resplendent, O king, like Śakra contending with Bala in battle.

sanskrit: duryodhano dhanuś chittvā dhṛṣṭadyumnasya saṃyuge athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Duryodhana, having cut the bow of Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the fight, then pierced him, his bow severed, with keen arrows.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi samare pragṛhya paramāyudham rājānaṃ yodhayām āsa paśyatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna too, taking up a supreme weapon in the battle, gave fight to the king before the eyes of all the bowmen.
